summary: "Guardians of Astro-Health" addresses astronaut bone mineral density loss by integrating TENG micro-motion/breathing energy harvesters, silicon-carbon batteries, and sweat biomarker patches. Continuous AI data matching enables predictive alerts, optimizing in-situ countermeasures and telemedical reviews to protect space crews and terrestrial osteoporosis patients.
details: "Guardians of Astro-Health" is an innovative biomedical monitoring and energy-harvesting ecosystem designed to protect astronauts from microgravity-induced bone mineral density loss during long-duration space missions. To solve deep-space power constraints, the project integrates dual Triboelectric Nanogenerator (TENG) modules that convert body micro-motions, mechanics, and breathing into electrical energy, regulated by a Power Management Integrated Circuit and stored in an ultra-thin, high-density silicon-carbon battery. For diagnostics, an integrated biosensor patch tracks accelerometric movement and sweat microfluidics (Ca^2+ and ALP), while continuous software algorithms match this data against pre-launch DEXA baselines to evaluate skeletal strain. If critical demineralization thresholds are crossed, a 3-tier alert protocol triggers in-situ countermeasures or Mission Control interventions for early return planning. By replacing bulky diagnostic hardware, mitigating dangerous orbital medical evacuations, and even adapting triboelectric concepts to harness electrostatic Martian winds, the project effectively protects Artemis and Mars crews while offering valuable terrestrial applications for severe osteoporosis patients.
